summary: A short meeting notice from Jon Postel for a one-day meeting on Remote Job Entry protocols in the ARPANET, held at UCLA on April 21, 1972. Attendees were asked to read earlier reports by Alex McKenzie and Kampe from a previous RJE meeting. It also points to the data and file transfer protocols as relevant.

eli5.summary: A teacher announces a meeting where people will talk about how to send big jobs to far-away computers. Everyone is asked to read the earlier notes first.

subtitle: A working meeting to design remote job entry protocols

tldr.problem: The ARPANET community needed to define a standard way for computers to submit jobs remotely to distant machines and receive results back.
tldr.mechanism: Jon Postel announced a one-day working meeting at UCLA on April 21, 1972, bringing together network researchers to discuss Remote Job Entry (RJE) protocol specifications.
tldr.outcome: This meeting was part of a series that defined RJE standards, allowing different computers on the ARPANET to submit batch jobs to each other reliably.

today: RFC 324 is a historical meeting notice for early ARPANET protocol development. RJE became an important capability on the ARPANET, allowing batch job submission, though modern cloud computing and remote execution have superseded these specific protocols.

sections.title: The RJE Working Meeting
sections.content: On April 3, 1972, Jon Postel of UCLA announced a working meeting to discuss Remote Job Entry (RJE) protocols for the ARPANET. The meeting would be held on Friday, April 21, 1972, from 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. in the Ackerman Student Union Building at UCLA.
sections.eli5: Jon Postel called a meeting to talk about how computers could send jobs to each other on the network.

sections.title: What the Meeting Covered
sections.content: Attendees were expected to have read earlier reports on RJE work by Alex McKenzie (from February 25, 1972) and Kampe (from March 8, 1972) from a previous RJE meeting. The current meeting would also consider the Data and File Transfer protocols as relevant to RJE, since moving jobs and their results required reliable data transfer mechanisms.
sections.eli5: People had to do homework first, reading what was said about this before. The meeting would also talk about how to move files, since that is part of sending jobs.

sections.title: Participation
sections.content: The RFC invited prospective attendees to confirm their attendance by contacting Bryna Lang at (213) 825-2368. This brief notice was a typical way the early ARPANET community coordinated protocol development, with working groups gathering to debate and agree on technical details.
sections.eli5: People signed up to come by calling a number. It was how the early network fixed how computers should talk to each other.
